Document Description: The Project site is located at on an approximately 23. 75-acre site comprised of five parcels located at 3050 Zanker Road, 2840-2880 Junction Avenue, and 411 East Plumeria Drive. The project proposes to demolish all 5 existing office/research and development buildings and develop three new speculative industrial buildings, totaling approximately 328,701 square feet of warehouse space and 72,600 square feet of office space. The proposed buildings would cover approximately 39 percent of the total project site and would have a maximum height of approximately 47 feet. Document Title: Temporary Moratorium on Data Center Development, Establishment, Intensification, and Expansion
Document Description: Adoption of an ordinance to enact a temporary moratorium on the development of data centers in the City of San Diego. Data centers present a threat to public safety, health and welfare, and a moratorium provides the City with time to study, consider, and potentially adopt regulations to address whether, where, and under what conditions data centers should be allowed within the City.
Project Title: Temporary Moratorium on Data Center Development, Establishment, Intensification, and Expansion
Contact Authority: City of San Diego City Planning Department
NOE Exempt Citation: CEQA Guidelines Section 15308 (Actions by Regulatory Agencies for the Protection of the Environment)
NOE Reasons for Exemption:
The City of San Diego conducted an environmental review that determined the project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3), as CEQA only applies to projects which have the potential for causing a
significant effect on the environment As the proposed temporary moratorium would not result in any direct or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical changes in the environment, it would not be subject to CEQA. Furthermore, the project would not have the potential for causing a significant effect on the environment pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15308 (Actions by Regulatory Agencies for the Protection of the Environment), which applies to actions taken by regulatory agencies to maintain, restore, enhance, or protect the environment; and where the exceptions listed in CEQA Guidelines Section 15300.2 would not apply in that no cumulative impacts were identified; no significant effects on the environment were identified; the project is not adjacent to a scenic highway; no historical resources would be affected by the action; and the project was not identified on a list of hazardous waste sites
pursuant to Section 65962.5 of the Government Code. R-317004

Document Title: Amendments to BMC Title 17 (Zoning) For Data Centers
Document Description: Amend portions of Title 17 (Zoning) of the Benicia Municipal Code for Data Centers. The proposed amendments would establish zoning regulations for Data Centers and make minor clean up amendments. The City Council conducted a public hearing, waived the first reading and introduced the ordinance during a duly noticed public hearing on October 20, 2026.
Project Title: Amendments to BMC Title 17 (Zoning) For Data Centers
NOE Reasons for Exemption: This project is categorically exempt pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines Sections 15301 and 15305 which apply to existing facilities and minor alterations to land use limitations. The proposed amendments on their own do not have the potential to result in significant environmental impacts as they establish a new use classification that increases review and analysis for proposed uses and establish standards to avoid adverse impacts. New uses or development proposed pursuant to this amendment would be subject to CEQA review on a case by-case basis to ensure that any significant environmental impacts are adequately addressed.

Document Description:
The Project includes the construction of an approximately 18-acre bulk substation within a 44 acre parcel. The proposed substation would convert high voltage from 230,000-volt (230kV) transmission lines to 69,000-volt (69kV) through transformers for local distribution into residential and commercial customers along the Jackson Highway corridor. Key features of the new substation include installation of new electrical equipment, a control building, driveway access, site fencing, lighting, stormwater drainage, and utilities. SMUD will also grade the remaining 26 acres for drainage improvements and maintain temporary soil storage south of the substation footprint. The substation will retain a 200-foot setback from Jackson Road and Excelsior Road.
 
The Project also includes construction of new or modified overhead power lines that would link the substation to the existing electrical grid. Planned overhead line improvements involve constructing approximately 0.7 miles of new 69kV overhead lines and converting approximately 5.35 miles of existing 12,000-volt (12kV) pole and overhead lines to single-circuit 69kV overhead lines with a 12kV underbuild.
Location Cross Streets: southeast corner of Excelsior Road and Jackson Road

Document Title: Twain Harte Creek Sewer Line Crossing Emergency Repair Project
Document Description: Streambank erosion undermined and exposed a sewer line crossing at Twain Harte Creek very near Twain Harte Lake. Remove, replace, and extend existing concrete encasement; remove woody debris; and fill undermined voids and create cutoff wall to reduce risk of sewer line failure and sanitary sewer overflow before heavy writer rains increase risk. up to 9 cubic yards of concrete net fill may be used.
Project Title: Twain Harte Creek Sewer Line Crossing Emergency Repair Project
Location Waterways: Twain Harte Creek, Twain Harte Lake
NOE Reasons for Exemption: Recent routine inspection discovered the undermined encasement and exposed sewer line. This damage leaves the sewer line highly susceptible to failure during high stream flows, which would cause a sewer overflow into Twain Harte Creek and Twain Harte Lake. Further undermining and failure is considered imminent due to the developing strong El Nino event, threatening life and property for the residents of Twain Harte.
